name: open-data-cube
summary: Earth observation and raster analytics stack for turning imagery collections into analysis-ready data cubes.
why_it_matters: Open Data Cube preserves useful remote-sensing capability knowledge, but there is no current validated geospatial workflow that warrants actively supporting the full stack.
when_to_use: A future scenario needs satellite imagery indexing and time-series analysis.
Operators want analysis-ready geospatial data cubes rather than ad hoc raster handling.
The workflow depends on earth-observation analytics across large datasets.

platform_support.notes: The stack can be containerized, but realistic support depends on storage, dataset ingestion, and geospatial service validation.

prerequisites: Persistent storage for large imagery datasets
Clear operator workflow for indexing and export
implementation_notes: Promotion should validate a concrete ingest-and-query workflow.
Keep data-management concerns separate from geospatial visualization concerns.
Avoid broad platform support without real scenario demand.
operational_notes: Storage growth and ingest throughput dominate operations.
Validation should include a known dataset and query path.
Backup strategy needs to cover both metadata and content.
risks: The stack is heavy and easy to keep around speculatively.
Without active scenarios, maintenance cost outweighs value.
